newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh privatises cargo handling at port.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh privatises cargo handling at port.

text.p: Bangladesh on Monday began allowing port users to operate private equipment to speed up cargo handling, in a move aimed at eventual privatisation of the country's main Chittagong port, port officials said. "This has ended a battle between the government and the port workers over the use of private handling equipment by port users," one official said.

Port officials said there was no formal timetable for the full privatisation of the port. It would occur in phases. The government-employed port workers fear privatisation of the port may cost them their jobs but port officials said existing employees would not lose their jobs.

They said government leaders, including Shipping Minister A.S.M. Abdur Rab and Chittagong City Mayor A.B.M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, persuaded the workers to withdraw their opposition to private sector activities at the port. "The presence of a strong private sector is essential at the port which handles 80 percent of the country's external trade," Rab told the Port Users Forum (PUF) on Sunday.

The PUF is a body of stevedores, clearing and forwarding agents and shipping agencies. They want to use their own equipment in jetties and container yards for loading and unloading, which the government in principle earlier agreed to allow.
The decision was delayed in the wake of protests by the port labour union.

But the 8,000 port employees supported the move after the government accepted demands for financial benefits, port officials said without elaborating. They said port users could now bring in their own straddle carriers and fork lifts to handle cargo. Port worker unions had protested against a recent directive by Chittagong Port Authority (CPA) executives allowing the use of private equipment.
The unions threatened to strike indefinitely unless the decision, taken at a meeting earlier this month at the office of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, was reversed.

Chittagong port, which handles 80 percent of the country's exports and imports, has faced repeated work disruptions over the past few months as rival trade unions fought over the use of private equipment.
